# LinkedIn post · LinkedIn Leverage Toolkit carousel

Attach `out/LinkedIn-Leverage-Toolkit_carousel.pdf` as a document.
Document title (LinkedIn asks for one on upload): LinkedIn Leverage Toolkit: a practical guide built from real experiments

---

857,763 impressions in 13 months, and 75% of them came from people outside my network.

I'm not a LinkedIn expert. I kept testing things and writing down what happened.

This is that list, cleaned up. It's version 2 of a guide I first wrote in March.

It covers:
→ How LinkedIn decides who sees your post
→ What worked for me, and what didn't
→ The formats that perform, ranked
→ The tools I use, and when to be careful with automation
→ A profile checklist with 16 sections
→ Five workflows, from post to pipeline
→ The mistakes I already made

The lesson that mattered most: don't try to plan your niche from day one. Mine showed up when a job post for Design roles got unusually high engagement. That told me my audience cared about design community content, so I leaned into it.

Yes, it's 33 slides, and inside I recommend five to ten. It's a guide, so I made an exception.

Two people I learn from are in there too: @Matt Lakajev and @Ruben Hassid.

What's one thing you've tested on LinkedIn that actually worked?
